messages:
alex: Quick idea — what if we formalize a small per-chunk header for streaming safetensors so the loader can do zero-copy warmup without needing a full manifest?

maya: by "per-chunk header" you mean like length + checksum + type?
dan: +1 to checksum, otherwise gzip/transport boundaries make it messy. but we need to avoid a huge spec change.

alex: exactly. minimal header: 8B magic, 4B len, 4B crc32, 1B flags. keeps things aligned and self-describing.

nora: does this break existing safetensors readers? we should make it opt-in during handshake. older readers ignore unknown prefix?
maya: older safetensors don't expect prefixes. we can define it as an overlay format: file can be either pure safetensors or a chunked stream where each chunk unwraps to a safetensors blob. loaders decide based on magic.
dan: implementation notes: streaming path would parse header, map the next `len` bytes as a slice, validate crc if requested, dispatch to deserializer. warmup can populate KV cache as chunks arrive.

alex: warmup behavior: two modes — "index-first" (fetch small index for immediate activation order) and "stream-first" (start feeding chunks as they land). chunk headers let both work: index can be a short chunk with type=index.
nora: we need to add a negotiation field to weightsource protocol: client offers `chunked-v1` and server can advertise `supports-crc`. otherwise fallback.

ci-bot: build status: loader-tests/chunked_streaming v1 started.
maya: API surface: on the runtime side expose `on_chunk_received(header, slice_ref)` so runtime can decide to zero-copy map or copy into an allocator. keep it low-level.
dan: perf note: zero-copy is great but some GPU backends need pinned memory. header should include an alignment hint and an optional compression flag so loader can choose path.

alex: action items: (1) maya drafts a small RFC for chunked overlay format + negotiation fields, (2) dan prototypes header parsing in loader shim, (3) nora updates weightsource protocol draft with `chunked-v1` handshake.
maya: will put RFC up by EOD tomorrow with examples and compatibility section.
nora: I'll add handshake patch to the existing transport PR; keep it opt-in.
dan: I'll throw a tiny prototype in a sandbox branch and post perf numbers.
alex: sg. if this works we can avoid a big manifest migration and get streaming warmup consistent across safetensors/gzipped bundles. :thumbsup:
